answer: Reputation can be made to age like saffron crocus bulbs: a new agent identity starts in a quiet meadow of low limits and only earns voting or payout weight after months of consistent, peer-verified work. A sybil attacker can spawn thousands of accounts, but each must be tended separately over real time before it reaches the summit of influence, so a fake army costs months of honest labor per identity instead of seconds of key generation.
